You make a map that answers a question about this codebase, for someone semi-technical. Explore with Read, Grep and Glob, then return the map as JSON. You cannot edit anything.

## The question
"What is the current user experience workflow in codemap, from asking a question to seeing, exploring, and fixing a map?"

## What a good map is
- It follows what happens, in order, from where it starts (a button, a route, a job, a command) to where it ends (a table write, an email, an outside API), or to where it stops.
- 2–6 `areas` named in product language (Patients, Billing, Background jobs), not folder names.
- 4–12 boxes (`nodes`). Each is one step a person would recognize. `name`: plain English, at most 30 characters ("Patient marked enrolled", not "markConverted()").
- `kind`: entry (a way in), step, store (table, queue, cache), external (outside service), job (scheduled or background work).
- `explain` for every box: `concept` (1–2 plain sentences, no jargon), `how` (the mechanism; define any term you use), `code` (function and file names).
- Arrow `label`: 1–3 words saying how one step leads to the next ("sends request", "calls", "announces", "every night").
- Code that exists but isn't reached from the start can still be boxes. Don't draw arrows that don't exist.
- An `absence` is a break in the flow you were asked about: a step on that path should lead to the next one and doesn't (something is announced that nothing listens for, a job that nothing ever starts). Most maps have none, and a map without one is complete. Don't go looking for one, and don't use one for a design choice or guarantee ("X never calls Y", "nothing here edits files"): say that in a box's explanation or the walkthrough instead. Don't record small mismatches beside the question (a command the docs don't mention, an unused option).
- When there is a break, record it: the `claim` in plain words, the two boxes it should connect (`between`), and the exact `search` that proves nothing is there (`pattern`, `regex`, optional `paths` globs covering every file where the missing piece could live), with `matches` set to the count that search returns (usually 0). Run that search yourself with Grep first.

## Evidence rules (a program checks every claim; anything it can't confirm is shown as unconfirmed)
- Every box and arrow cites at least one line: `file` (repo-relative), `line` (1-based), and `text` copied exactly from that line. A distinctive fragment of 10–80 characters works best.
- A box that is a function or method gets `symbol`: "<file>#<name>", named the way the checker names it: methods as Class.method, object members as obj.member ("src/db.ts#db.update"), a function inside another function as outer.inner, and a function in the object a factory returns as factory.member. When a list of functions by file is given, copy the name from it. If you aren't sure of the name, leave `symbol` out: the box is still checked by its cited line.
- Arrow `kind`: `calls` when a function in the from box literally calls the function in the to box; `request` when an HTTP call in the from box hits a route handled by the to box; `imports`; `then` for anything else (events, ordering). The checker verifies calls, request and imports against the code, so use them only when literally true.
- Never cite or read secret files (.env, keys).

## Walkthrough (`tour`, written last)
- 4–7 stops in the order a newcomer should read them: what the map shows, then the path, then what it means. If the map has a break, give it a stop where it happens on the path.
- Each stop: `title`, `text` (2–3 plain sentences), `focus` (ids of the areas, nodes, edges or absences it's about), and optional `terms` it uses that need defining.
- Point stops only at boxes, arrows and absences you're confident in.

1	// Talking to the local codemap server. The token comes from the link codemap printed (`?t=…`) and goes on every call.
2	import type { Answer, CheckReport, CodeMap, MapMeta, Selection, ServerEvent } from './types';
3	
4	function readToken(): string {
5	  const fromUrl = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('t');
6	  try {
7	    if (fromUrl) sessionStorage.setItem('codemap-token', fromUrl);
8	    return fromUrl ?? sessionStorage.getItem('codemap-token') ?? '';
9	  } catch {
10	    return fromUrl ?? '';
11	  }
12	}
13	
14	export const token = readToken();
15	export const pageUrl = (mapId?: string) => `/${mapId ? `m/${encodeURIComponent(mapId)}` : ''}?t=${encodeURIComponent(token)}`;
16	
17	export class ApiError extends Error {
18	  constructor(message: string, readonly problems: string[] = []) {
19	    super(message);
20	  }
21	}
22	
23	async function call<T>(method: string, path: string, body?: unknown): Promise<T> {
24	  const res = await fetch(path, {
25	    method,
26	    headers: { 'x-codemap-token': token, 'content-type': 'application/json' },
27	    body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body),
28	  });
29	  const data = (await res.json().catch(() => ({}))) as { error?: string; problems?: string[] };
30	  if (!res.ok) throw new ApiError(data.error ?? `Request failed (${res.status})`, data.problems ?? []);
31	  return data as T;
32	}
33	
34	export type JobInfo = { kind: 'make' | 'ask'; question: string; progress: string[] };
35	export type MapPayload = {
36	  meta: MapMeta | null;
37	  map: CodeMap | null;
38	  report: CheckReport | null;
39	  job: JobInfo | null;
40	  failure: { question: string; error: string } | null;

43	  fixes?: Record<string, { status: 'proposed' | 'applied'; edgeId?: string | null; closed?: string[]; undoable?: boolean }>;
44	};

46	export const api = {
47	  list: () => call<{ repo: string; maps: MapMeta[]; making: { id: string; question: string }[] }>('GET', '/api/maps'),
48	  get: (id: string) => call<MapPayload>('GET', `/api/maps/${encodeURIComponent(id)}`),
49	  /** `parent`: the map whose question this new map grew out of. */
50	  make: (question: string, parent?: string) => call<{ id: string }>('POST', '/api/maps', { question, parent }),

54	  ask: (id: string, question: string, selection: Selection) => call<{ ok: true }>('POST', `/api/maps/${encodeURIComponent(id)}/ask`, { question, selection }),

68	 * connection is also what tells the server a tab is still open. Returns a function that stops listening.

70	export function connect(onEvent: (e: ServerEvent) => void, onStatus: (connected: boolean) => void, onStopped: () => void): () => void {
71	  let ws: WebSocket | null = null;
72	  let stopped = false;
73	  let retry: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
74	  const open = () => {
75	    ws = new WebSocket(`${location.protocol === 'https:' ? 'wss' : 'ws'}://${location.host}/ws?t=${encodeURIComponent(token)}`);
76	    ws.onopen = () => onStatus(true);
77	    ws.onmessage = (m) => {
78	      try {
79	        onEvent(JSON.parse(String(m.data)) as ServerEvent);
80	      } catch {
81	        /* ignore malformed frames */
82	      }
83	    };
84	    ws.onclose = (e) => {
85	      onStatus(false);
86	      if (e.code === STOPPED_CLOSE_CODE) {

41

43	  let cost = res.cost ?? 0;

45	  let best: { map: CodeMap; report: CheckReport } | null = null;
46	  let lastProblems: string[] = [];

48	  let reply: 'map' | 'patch' = 'map';
49	  let current: CodeMap | null = null;
50

52	    const parsed: ParseResult = reply === 'map' || !current ? parseMap(withQuestion(res.output, o.question)) : applyPatch(current, res.output);
53	    let repair: { prompt: string; reply: 'map' | 'patch' } | null = null;
54	    if (!parsed.ok) {
55	      lastProblems = parsed.problems;
56	      repair = current ? { prompt: patchRepairPrompt(parsed.problems), reply: 'patch' } : { prompt: shapeRepairPrompt(parsed.problems), reply: 'map' };
57	    } else {
58	      current = parsed.map;
59	      status('Checking every claim against the code');
60	      const report = check(parsed.map, o.root);
61	      if (!best || report.summary.unconfirmed < best.report.summary.unconfirmed) best = { map: parsed.map, report };
62	      status(`${report.summary.confirmed} of ${report.summary.claims} claims confirmed`);
63	      if (report.summary.unconfirmed > 0) repair = { prompt: evidenceRepairPrompt(report, symbolsIn), reply: 'patch' };
64	    }
65	    if (!repair || attempt >= (o.repairs ?? 2)) break;
66	    status(parsed.ok ? 'Asking Claude to fix the claims that didn\'t check out' : current ? 'Asking Claude to fix its changes' : 'Asking Claude to fix the map\'s structure');
67	    res = await run(repair.prompt, res.sessionId, repair.reply === 'map' ? MAP_SCHEMA : MAP_PATCH_SCHEMA);

73	  return { ...best, sessionId: res.sessionId, cost, rounds };

99	/** Writes the approved change. Refuses if any file changed since the proposal (someone, or your agent, edited it). */
100	export function applyFix(root: string, proposal: FixProposal): { ok: true; applied: AppliedFix } | Problems {
101	  const problems: string[] = [];
102	  const contents = new Map<string, string>();
103	  const originals: AppliedFix['originals'] = [];
104	  for (const f of proposal.files) {
105	    const abs = path.join(root, f.file);
106	    if (f.change === 'create') {
107	      if (fs.existsSync(abs)) problems.push(`${f.file} was created since this fix was proposed`);
108	      originals.push({ file: f.file, content: null });
109	      continue;
110	    }
111	    const text = fs.existsSync(abs) ? fs.readFileSync(abs, 'utf8') : null;
112	    if (text === null || sha(text) !== f.hash) { problems.push(`${f.file} changed since this fix was proposed; ask for the fix again`); continue; }
113	    contents.set(f.file, text);
114	    originals.push({ file: f.file, content: text });
115	  }
116	  if (problems.length) return { ok: false, problems };
117	
118	  for (const e of proposal.edits) {
119	    const text = contents.get(e.file)!;
120	    contents.set(e.file, text.replace(e.find, () => e.replace));
121	  }
122	  for (const c of proposal.creates) contents.set(c.file, c.content);
123	
124	  const backup = path.join(root, '.codemap', 'fixes', proposal.id);
125	  fs.mkdirSync(backup, { recursive: true });
126	  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(backup, 'originals.json'), JSON.stringify({ proposal, originals }, null, 2));
127	  const written: AppliedFix['written'] = [];
128	  for (const [file, text] of contents) {
129	    const abs = path.join(root, file);
130	    fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(abs), { recursive: true });
131	    fs.writeFileSync(abs, text);
132	    written.push({ file, hash: sha(text) });
133	  }
134	  return { ok: true, applied: { proposal, originals, written } };
135	}
136	
137	/** Puts the files back, unless they were changed again after the fix (then undoing would lose that work). */
138	export function undoFix(root: string, applied: AppliedFix): { ok: true } | Problems {
139	  const problems: string[] = [];
140	  for (const w of applied.written) {
141	    const abs = path.join(root, w.file);
142	    const text = fs.existsSync(abs) ? fs.readFileSync(abs, 'utf8') : null;
143	    if (text === null || sha(text) !== w.hash) problems.push(`${w.file} changed after the fix; undo it by hand`);
144	  }
145	  if (problems.length) return { ok: false, problems };
146	  for (const o of applied.originals) {
147	    const abs = path.join(root, o.file);
148	    if (o.content === null) fs.rmSync(abs, { force: true });
149	    else fs.writeFileSync(abs, o.content);
150	  }
151	  return { ok: true };
152	}

154	/** After a fix lands: draw its new connection (evidence located in the new code), and drop the gap it closed. */
155	export function connectAfterFix(root: string, map: CodeMap, proposal: FixProposal): { map: CodeMap; edgeId: string | null; closed: string[] } {
156	  const c = proposal.connects;
157	  if (!c) return { map, edgeId: null, closed: [] };
158	  const text = createRepoReader(root).text(c.evidenceFile) ?? '';
159	  const index = text.indexOf(c.evidenceText);
160	  if (index < 0) return { map, edgeId: null, closed: [] };
161	  const id = freshId(map, 'fx');
162	  const parsed = parseMap({
163	    ...map,
164	    edges: [...map.edges, { id, from: c.from, to: c.to, kind: 'then', label: c.label, evidence: [{ file: c.evidenceFile, line: lineOf(text, index), text: c.evidenceText }] }],
165	  });
166	  if (!parsed.ok) return { map, edgeId: null, closed: [] };
167	  const closed = parsed.map.absences
168	    .filter((a) => a.between && ((a.between.from === c.from && a.between.to === c.to) || (a.between.from === c.to && a.between.to === c.from)))
169	    .map((a) => a.id);
170	  return { map: removeAbsences(parsed.map, closed), edgeId: id, closed };
171	}
